senses.gloss:
Glau occurs in the Atharvaveda and in the aitareya brāhmaṇa as the name of some symptom of a disease, probably, as Bloomfield thinks, ‘boils.’ In the one passage of the Vājasaneyi Saṃhita, where it is found the sense is obscure, some part of the sacrificial victim being perhaps meant.
Cf. galunta.
Foot notes vi. 83, 3.
i. 25.
Proceedings of the American Oriental Society, October, 1887, xv.; Hymns of the Atharvaveda, 17, 503; Whitney, Translation of the Atharvaveda, 343.
xxv. 8; Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, iii. 15, 7.
St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v.; Ludwig, Translation of the Rigveda, 3, 500, takes glau as ‘owl.’
